name: DeepSeek
description: DeepSeek's open-weight AI models and free chat platform. The current flagship is DeepSeek-V4 (V4-Pro and V4-Flash, released 2026-04-24, MIT-licensed) with a 1M-token context window and native multimodal image understanding; the earlier DeepSeek-R1 reasoning model remains available. Known for leading open-model agentic coding and extremely cost-efficient inference.

writing-chat.summary: DeepSeek provides a free conversational chat interface and API. The flagship DeepSeek-V4 (V4-Pro and V4-Flash) offers a built-in Thinking / Non-Thinking mode toggle and a 1M-token context window; the older DeepSeek-R1 reasoning model is still available.

subFeatures.name: DeepSeek Chat (V4)
subFeatures.description: Web-based chat powered by DeepSeek-V4 with multi-turn conversation, markdown rendering, and code highlighting

subFeatures.name: DeepThink (Thinking Mode)
subFeatures.description: Toggle deep reasoning that shows step-by-step thinking for math, logic, and complex analysis; built into V4 and also available via the older R1 model

subFeatures.name: 1M-Token Context
subFeatures.description: Both V4-Pro and V4-Flash support a 1M-token context window, a large increase over the 64K context of the earlier V3/R1 models

limitations: Web interface less polished than ChatGPT or Claude
English-primary but optimized for Chinese as well — other languages less supported
Thinking mode is slower due to chain-of-thought generation
Service availability may vary by region with occasional capacity throttling at peak

pricingTiers.details: Free access to DeepSeek chat with V4 (DeepThink and Search toggles)
Per-token rates published on the official pricing page; V4-Flash positioned as a highly cost-effective option. See platform.deepseek.com/api-pricing for current rates
DeepSeek-V4-Pro and V4-Flash weights released under MIT license on Hugging Face — free to self-host

versionHistory.changes: Current flagship (2026-04-24): V4-Pro (1.6T total / ~49B active) and V4-Flash (284B total / ~13B active) MoE models, 1M-token context, Thinking/Non-Thinking modes, MIT license
Reasoning model matching o1-class performance; now the older model, superseded by V4 for most uses
671B MoE model (now obsolete; replaced by V4)

research.summary: DeepSeek offers web search capabilities in its chat interface and excels at analyzing and reasoning about complex topics, though its web search is less mature than ChatGPT or Perplexity.

subFeatures.name: Web Search
subFeatures.description: Search the web from within DeepSeek chat to find current information and cite sources

subFeatures.name: Deep Reasoning Analysis
subFeatures.description: Use R1's chain-of-thought reasoning to analyze complex research questions, break down problems, and synthesize information

limitations: Web search less comprehensive than Perplexity or ChatGPT browse
No autonomous multi-step research agent
Search results may be biased toward Chinese-language sources
No dedicated research report generation feature

pricingTiers.details: Web search included in free chat
No built-in web search in API — requires external integration

versionHistory.changes: Web search integration in DeepSeek chat interface

file-analysis.summary: DeepSeek chat supports file uploads for analysis including documents, images, and code files, with the R1 model providing detailed reasoning about file contents.

subFeatures.name: Document Upload and Analysis
subFeatures.description: Upload PDFs, text files, and documents for DeepSeek to read, summarize, and answer questions about

subFeatures.name: Native Image & Video Understanding
subFeatures.description: DeepSeek-V4 integrates image and video understanding trained in during pre-training (native multimodality), analyzing diagrams, screenshots, and photographs — a capability absent in V3

subFeatures.name: Code File Analysis
subFeatures.description: Read, explain, and debug uploaded code files with detailed reasoning

limitations: File size limits more restrictive than competitors
No sandboxed code execution environment for data analysis
Spreadsheet and CSV analysis limited to text-based parsing
Multimodal understanding is built into V4; older V3 was text-only

pricingTiers.details: File uploads and image analysis included in free chat
Multimodal input supported in API at standard token pricing

versionHistory.changes: Native multimodal image and video understanding trained in during pre-training
Document upload support in chat interface

document-creation.summary: DeepSeek generates text-based documents, technical reports, and structured content through its chat interface, with R1 excelling at detailed technical and mathematical documentation.

subFeatures.name: Technical Document Generation
subFeatures.description: Generate technical reports, code documentation, and analysis documents with detailed reasoning and mathematical notation

subFeatures.name: Structured Output
subFeatures.description: Produce well-formatted markdown content including tables, code blocks, LaTeX math, and structured lists

limitations: No dedicated document editor or workspace
No export to Word, PDF, or other formats
No collaborative editing features
Output limited to text formats

pricingTiers.details: Full text generation in chat
Structured output and JSON mode via API

versionHistory.changes: Stronger long-form and technical document generation with Thinking mode
Enhanced technical writing with chain-of-thought reasoning

image-generation.summary: DeepSeek-V4 is natively multimodal and understands images, but image generation is not a confirmed user-facing feature in the consumer app. DeepSeek remains focused on text, reasoning, and code, with image understanding (not creation).

subFeatures.name: No Confirmed Image Generation
subFeatures.description: DeepSeek-V4 adds native image understanding, but text-to-image generation is not a confirmed feature in the chat app — DeepSeek's strength remains text, reasoning, and code

limitations: No confirmed image generation feature in the consumer app
Native multimodality covers image understanding, not image creation
Cannot reliably create visual assets or illustrations

pricingTiers.details: Image generation not offered as a confirmed feature

versionHistory.changes: Adds native image understanding; image generation not confirmed in the consumer app

prototyping.summary: DeepSeek-V4 leads open models on agentic coding benchmarks and is explicitly optimized for developer toolchains like Claude Code, making it effective for prototyping through chat and API, though it lacks its own code execution environment.

subFeatures.name: Agentic Coding (V4)
subFeatures.description: DeepSeek-V4 leads open models on agentic coding benchmarks and is tuned for agentic developer toolchains such as Claude Code

subFeatures.name: Code Reasoning (Thinking Mode)
subFeatures.description: Use V4's Thinking mode (or the older R1 model) for complex algorithmic problems, debugging, and multi-step code architecture decisions

subFeatures.name: Open-Weight Model Access
subFeatures.description: Run DeepSeek-V4 locally or on custom infrastructure under MIT license for private prototyping without sending code to external servers

limitations: No sandboxed code execution environment
No live preview or interactive code runner
No IDE integration beyond API access
Local deployment requires significant GPU resources for full models

pricingTiers.details: Code generation in chat with DeepSeek-V4
Extremely cost-efficient code generation via API (V4-Pro / V4-Flash)
MIT-licensed open weights for local deployment

versionHistory.changes: Leads open models on agentic coding; optimized for Claude Code and similar toolchains
Reasoning model with strong code generation and debugging
Specialized coding model with strong benchmark results

personalization.summary: DeepSeek has minimal personalization features — no custom instructions, memory, or persistent preference system in the web interface.

subFeatures.name: System Prompts (API)
subFeatures.description: API users can set system prompts to customize model behavior, but the web interface has no equivalent personalization

limitations: No custom instructions in the web interface
No memory or persistent preferences
No custom bot or persona creation
API-only system prompt customization

pricingTiers.details: No personalization features
System prompts for behavior customization

persistent-context.summary: DeepSeek maintains conversation history within the web app and DeepSeek-V4 offers a 1M-token context for long single sessions, but it still lacks any persistent cross-session memory or projects.

subFeatures.name: Conversation History
subFeatures.description: Saved conversations accessible from the sidebar, with the ability to continue or reference previous discussions

subFeatures.name: 1M-Token Context Window
subFeatures.description: DeepSeek-V4 supports a 1M-token context window (up from 64K on V3/R1), allowing extended conversations and large documents within a single session

limitations: No persistent cross-session memory system (still absent as of May 2026)
No projects or saved knowledge base for persistent context
Conversation search limited to basic text matching
No project or workspace organization

pricingTiers.details: Conversation history included
Context management handled by API consumer

versionHistory.changes: Conversation history and management in web interface

agents.summary: DeepSeek supports agentic use through its API with function calling and tool use, enabling developers to build autonomous agents. The chat interface does not have built-in agent features.

subFeatures.name: Function Calling (API)
subFeatures.description: API support for function calling and tool use, enabling developers to build agents that interact with external systems

subFeatures.name: Open-Source Agent Frameworks
subFeatures.description: DeepSeek models are widely used in open-source agent frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI) due to cost efficiency and open weights

limitations: No built-in agent features in the web interface
No autonomous task execution in chat
No browser automation or computer use capabilities
Agent building requires external framework and development effort

pricingTiers.details: No agent features in web interface
Function calling at standard API token pricing
Agent frameworks with local model deployment

versionHistory.changes: Tool use and function calling support in V3 API

connectors.summary: DeepSeek connects to external systems primarily through its OpenAI-compatible API, making it a drop-in replacement in existing tool chains. No native third-party integrations exist in the web interface.

subFeatures.name: OpenAI-Compatible API
subFeatures.description: API follows OpenAI's format, enabling drop-in replacement in applications built for GPT models with minimal code changes

subFeatures.name: Open-Source Ecosystem
subFeatures.description: Available on Hugging Face and major inference platforms (vLLM, Ollama, Together AI), with broad ecosystem compatibility

limitations: No native third-party integrations in web interface
No plugin or extension ecosystem
No direct Google Drive, OneDrive, or cloud storage connectors
Integration requires API development or third-party tools

pricingTiers.details: OpenAI-compatible API at DeepSeek pricing
Free model weights with self-hosted infrastructure costs

versionHistory.changes: R1 open-source weights released on Hugging Face

dictation.summary: DeepSeek does not include voice input or dictation capabilities in its web interface or API.

subFeatures.name: Not Available
subFeatures.description: DeepSeek is a text-only platform with no voice or speech-to-text capabilities

limitations: No voice input or dictation support
No speech-to-text capabilities
No audio processing features
Text-only interaction in both web and API

pricingTiers.details: Not available
